answer: No, you should not be taking lisinopril. It was stopped on September 22, 2025, by Dr. Elena Marsh, because of a dry cough, and losartan 50 mg once daily was started in its place. At your June 15, 2026 visit the plan was to continue your current medicines, and losartan is the one listed as active now. The app that still shows lisinopril is most likely working from an older copy of your records: a March 2025 export from Kestrel Harbor Hospital still lists lisinopril as active, from before it was stopped. Please don't take lisinopril together with losartan, since taking both can raise potassium and strain the kidneys. Your potassium (4.2) and kidney function (eGFR 71) on June 15, 2026 were both normal. If you still have lisinopril at home, check with your pharmacy or Dr. Marsh before using it. You may also want to ask Dr. Marsh to record lisinopril as a cough intolerance, because your allergy list still shows it as active.

knowledge.says: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril and ARBs such as losartan should not be combined without a prescriber's direction, because the combination raises the risk of high potassium and kidney injury.
knowledge.guideline: Dual RAAS blockade is discouraged in routine practice (ACC/AHA hypertension guidance; ONTARGET/VA NEPHRON-D trial findings).
